headline: After morning fog, a coastal storm brings rain this afternoon into early Monday (under an inch for New York City, 1–2 inches farther east), and a bigger, more impactful coastal storm looks likely Wednesday night through Friday, with heavy rain on Thanksgiving, gusts of 35–45 mph and widespread coastal flooding.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Locally dense fog lingers until about 9 AM Sunday across the New York City metro, northern Long Island, southern Connecticut, much of northeastern New Jersey and the Lower Hudson Valley (it has already improved south of the Long Island Expressway), and then it will be unusually mild, with forecast highs of 61 at Bridgeport and 63 at Islip, close to the records of 64 for the date. Light rain could start late morning or early afternoon, then picks up mid-afternoon into the evening as low pressure moves up the coast, moderate to heavy at times especially in eastern areas. Rain totals keep trending down: less than an inch for the western half of the area including New York City, perhaps only a few tenths in the far west, and 1–2 inches over the eastern half, with the heaviest on eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut this evening and overnight. Winds turn east and then northeast at 10–15 mph with coastal gusts of 25–30 mph, plus a very low chance of brief 40–45 mph gusts right along the coast of eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut if the storm tracks close enough.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The rain moves out between about 1 and 4 AM Monday, with any leftover showers ending by daybreak, and Monday turns dry with west-northwest gusts of about 17–23 mph. A large, strong area of high pressure moves over the Northeast Tuesday into Wednesday, keeping those days dry. Wednesday night, east-northeast winds pick up with gusts of 23–35 mph possible, and rain may begin late as the next storm approaches from the south.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models continue to agree on a potentially large coastal storm Wednesday night through Thanksgiving and Friday, likely more impactful for wind and coastal flooding than Sunday's system, as it presses against the strong high pressure to the north. Gusts of 35–45 mph are possible sometime Thanksgiving Day or Thanksgiving night, and a period of moderate to heavy rain is likely on Thanksgiving, though the storm's fast movement should limit flooding from rain. The pattern is complex enough that small changes could shift the storm's strength, track and timing a lot, so forecasters are still monitoring it closely.

coast: With Monday morning's high tide, the south shore back bays of Nassau County may just touch minor flood levels at the most vulnerable spots, and a statement may eventually be needed, though a farther-east storm track and the storm's quick movement could keep water levels short. Tides run high with Tuesday's full moon, so many locations need less than a foot of extra water to reach minor flooding, and the current forecast supports widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, perhaps even localized major flooding, with the Wednesday night–Friday storm, along with beach flooding, erosion and overwash. On the water, locally dense fog with visibility of a mile or less is possible on Long Island Sound, the Long Island bays and New York Harbor until 9 AM; a Small Craft Advisory runs from 3 PM Sunday to 6 PM Monday for the near-shore ocean waters and from 6 PM Sunday to 6 AM Monday for the Sound, bays and harbor, and a Gale Warning covers the outer ocean waters from 6 PM Sunday to 6 AM Monday, with rough ocean seas lingering into Monday night. After a brief lull Tuesday afternoon and night, ocean gusts of 29–35 mph (25–30 knots) return by Wednesday afternoon, reaching gale force Wednesday night and storm force on Thursday, with gales reaching the Sound and bays late Wednesday night into Thursday. Waves could build to 12–20 feet on the ocean (occasionally 20–25 feet out east), 7–10 feet on western Block Island Sound east of Orient Point, and 4–6 feet on Long Island Sound and at the entrance to New York Harbor.
watch_for: Thanksgiving coastal storm: widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, possibly locally major, plus beach erosion and overwash, with gusts of 35–45 mph.
Track of today's storm: a farther-east track means less rain for New York City.
Possible minor flooding on the south shore back bays of Nassau County with Monday morning's high tide.
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in today's rain, though totals keep trending lower in the west, and models agree on a significant Thanksgiving storm, but its exact track, strength and timing remain uncertain because of a complex pattern.
